selection_firewall.candidate_origin: MC05 elimination class-gap search; theory and historical kinetics were paired by reaction identity, quantity typing, and condition overlap before any residual, chi, or ChemSA calculation

classification_basis: The computational source identifies a concerted mechanism through a six-membered transition state connecting ethyl acetate to ethylene and acetic acid.
The historical isotope-effect kinetic lineage independently supports beta C-H bond rupture in the transition state.
This physical family is distinct from the frozen FAM-ETHOXYHETEROCYCLE-ETHYLENE-ELIMINATION family and from the separately held ethyl-chloride HCl-elimination trail.

theory_source.authors: Diana C. Vargas, Sebastian Salazar, Jose R. Mora, Kevin M. Van Geem, Daniela Almeida Streitwieser
theory_source.title: Experimental and theoretical study of the thermal decomposition of ethyl acetate during fast pyrolysis
theory_source.method_selection_provenance: The paper states that omegaB97XD had previously shown useful transition-state geometry performance for other hydrogen-abstraction and radical-recombination reactions. No selection among same-reaction method variants by agreement with the selected 1960 target rate is disclosed.

stationary_point_validation.irc_connectivity: transition state connected by intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations to ethyl acetate reactant and ethylene plus acetic acid products

supplied_theory_quantity.type: theoretical activation energy Ea defined by the source as Ea = DeltaH_dagger + R*T

barrier_quantity.type: gas-phase activation enthalpy DeltaH_dagger = H_TS - H_react, reproducibly calculated from the source-supplied Ea using the source-defined relation Ea = DeltaH_dagger + R*T

primary_source.authors: Arthur T. Blades and P. W. Gilderson
primary_source.title: The secondary hydrogen isotope effects in the pyrolysis of ethyl-d5 acetate and ethyl acetate-d3
primary_source.rate_observable: first-order unimolecular ethyl-acetate disappearance / acetic-acid formation kinetic expression

independent_nbs_evaluation.source: NBS NSRDS 21, Kinetic Data on Gas Phase Unimolecular Reactions

independent_high_pressure_crosscheck.authors: Peter C. Beadle, David M. Golden, S. W. Benson
independent_high_pressure_crosscheck.statement: very-low-pressure pyrolysis results agree with previously determined high-pressure Arrhenius parameters log k_inf = 12.6 - 48.0/theta

observed_comparator.evaluation_note: The numerical k_inf is evaluated from the independently tabulated historical Arrhenius expression at the predeclared exact overlap temperature; residual magnitude was not used to select or promote the candidate.

condition_mapping.pressure_mapping_basis: The 1972 VLPP paper explicitly labels the earlier Arrhenius parameters as high-pressure parameters; the Atlas comparator therefore uses k_inf rather than a falloff-specific finite-pressure rate.

independence_basis: The selected primary rate experiment predates the 2020 calculation by sixty years and is from a separate research lineage.
The 2020 paper contains its own experimental pyrolysis dataset, but those same-study data are quarantined from comparator use in this trail.
The selected theory method is retained as reported; no method variant is chosen by smallest residual against the 1960 target.
The selected physical family is distinct from the frozen MC05 family and from the held ethyl-chloride trail.
quarantined_evidence: The 2020 paper's own experimental activation energy and rate model cannot serve as the independent comparator for its own theory.
The 1960/1970 rate-derived 48.0 kcal/mol Arrhenius activation energy cannot independently validate the observed rate from which it was derived.
No predicted/observed residual, chi value, or expected ChemSA agreement may vote on candidate selection or promotion.
